pluss::subsp::stats::ts::Garch11¶

Fits a GARCH(1, 1) model by maximum likelihood.

Signature¶

ts::Garch11Fit ts::Garch11::fit_mle(const pluss::Series& y, const ts::Garch11Options& options = {}, pluss::codem::Config cfg = {});

Construction¶

Garch11 has no instances: it is a namespace for the static fit_mle, which returns a Garch11Fit.

Methods¶

fit_mle¶

ts::Garch11Fit ts::Garch11::fit_mle(const pluss::Series& y, const ts::Garch11Options& options = {}, pluss::codem::Config cfg = {});

Fits the model to the return series y by maximising the Gaussian log-likelihood with a restarted Nelder–Mead search over an unconstrained parametrisation of the parameters. The variance recursion is h_t = ω + α e²_{t−1} + β h_{t−1} with ω > 0, α, β ≥ 0 and α + β < 1. The sample mean is removed first (unless demean is off) and held fixed. The recursion starts from the mean squared residual.

const pluss::Series& y

The return series in time order (at least 8 observations; a vector or an n × 1 matrix).

const ts::Garch11Options& options

Orders, starting values and search settings; see Garch11Options.

pluss::codem::Config cfg

Output configuration (dtype and platform of the returned series); computation is in double precision.

Returns. A Garch11Fit.

Errors. At least 8 observations are required. variance_floor, stationarity_margin, the iteration limits and nm_restarts must be positive and in range.

Practical Examples¶

Example 1¶

Fit the model to a series with volatility clustering and print the estimates.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.to_vec<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
// Returns whose variance responds more to negative shocks: h = 0.05 + (0.05 + 0.20 * 1[r < 0]) r_prev^2 + 0.75 h_prev.
Series returns(int n) {
  std::vector<double> r(n);
  double h = 0.5, prev = 0.0;
  for (int t = 0; t < n; ++t) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (t + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    const double z = (u - 0.5) * std::sqrt(12.0);
    h = 0.05 + (0.05 + (prev < 0 ? 0.20 : 0.0)) * prev * prev + 0.75 * h;
    r[t] = std::sqrt(h) * z;
    prev = r[t];
  }
  return pluss::make_series(r, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  const Series y = returns(1000);
  const auto fit = ts::Garch11::fit_mle(y);
  std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4) << "log-likelihood " << fit.loglik(y) << ", persistence " << fit.alpha + fit.beta << "\n";
}

Output

log-likelihood -1020.0632, persistence 0.8767

Example 2¶

A series that is too short is refused.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.to_vec<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
// Returns whose variance responds more to negative shocks: h = 0.05 + (0.05 + 0.20 * 1[r < 0]) r_prev^2 + 0.75 h_prev.
Series returns(int n) {
  std::vector<double> r(n);
  double h = 0.5, prev = 0.0;
  for (int t = 0; t < n; ++t) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (t + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    const double z = (u - 0.5) * std::sqrt(12.0);
    h = 0.05 + (0.05 + (prev < 0 ? 0.20 : 0.0)) * prev * prev + 0.75 * h;
    r[t] = std::sqrt(h) * z;
    prev = r[t];
  }
  return pluss::make_series(r, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  try {
    ts::Garch11::fit_mle(pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0}, f64));
  } catch (const std::exception&) {
    std::cout << "fewer than 8 observations are rejected\n";
  }
}

Output

fewer than 8 observations are rejected
